Jeongjun Choi

EmailGoogle ScholarGitHubCurriculum Vitae

I am a final-year Ph.D. student at Seoul National University, where I am fortunate to be advised by Prof. H. Jin Kim in the Laboratory for Autonomous Robotics Research (LARR). I also received my B.S. degree from Seoul National University under Prof. H. Jin Kim’s supervision.

My work on 3D generation began with human pose. In DiffuPose, I used diffusion to model the different 3D poses that could explain the same 2D keypoints. I then turned to language-guided scene synthesis. In SceneNAT, I studied how to generate a room layout that places the requested objects in the spatial relationships described by the user.

🔎Ongoing Research

  1. Humanoid in-context imitation from a single demonstration. My goal is for a humanoid to perform a new manipulation task from a single first-person video of a human demonstration, without task-specific retraining. I am exploring whether representing hand-object interactions as a graph can help the robot apply what it sees in the demonstration to unfamiliar objects and settings.
  2. Anticipating manipulation failures with video world models. I am working on ways for a robot to anticipate a manipulation failure while there is still time to act. I fine-tuned a video world model (NVIDIA Cosmos-Predict2.5) on robot manipulation trajectories to predict how objects might respond to the robot’s movements. I am exploring whether those predictions could help the robot decide when to continue and when to switch to a backup policy.
